paraphrase: Emptiness is explained by its characteristic, synonyms, their meaning, divisions and proof. Its characteristic is the non-existence of duality and the existence of that non-existence; it is neither existent nor non-existent, neither different from nor identical with (unreal imagination). Its synonyms are suchness, the limit of reality, the signless, the ultimate and the dharmadhātu — meaning unchanging, non-erroneous, cessation of signs, object of the noble ones' cognition, and cause of the noble qualities.

paraphrase: Emptiness is the non-existence of person and dharmas and the existence of that non-existence. If it were defiled, all embodied beings would be liberated; if it were pure, effort would be fruitless. It is neither defiled nor undefiled, neither pure nor impure, because the mind is luminous and the defilements are adventitious.

paraphrase: The cultivation of the four applications of mindfulness serves entry into the four truths, because of badness (the body), the cause of craving (feeling), the basis (mind) and non-delusion (dharmas).

paraphrase: Stability of mind for success in all aims arises from abandoning five faults and applying eight formations. The five faults are laziness, forgetting the instruction, sinking and agitation, non-application and (over-)application. The eight formations are the basis (desire-to-act), the based (effort), its cause (faith), its fruit (pliancy), non-forgetting of the object (mindfulness), noticing sinking and agitation (awareness), the application to remove them (intention), and calm flow when they have ceased (equanimity).
